# Incident report: order lookups return 500 for express orders placed near month-end

## 1. Summary

Since at least **19:51:14 UTC on 2026-09-30**, `GET /api/orders/{order_id}` has returned HTTP 500 (`ValueError: day is out of range for month`) for express order `express-1002`. The cause is a date bug in the delivery estimate. It fails every express order placed on a day where adding 2 to the day number goes past the end of the month. That includes express orders placed on 29 or 30 September, which is today. Affected customers can't view their order at all. The same function also breaks order creation and status updates for these orders (see Root cause). Standard orders are not affected.

## 2. Evidence

**Metrics (Prometheus), 19:48–20:18 UTC**
- 5 responses with 500 / `error.type=ValueError`, 1 with 200, 0 with 404. All 500s are on `http.route=/api/orders/{order_id}`.
- Minutes with 5xx responses: 19:52 (~4), 20:01 (~1), 20:18 (~1). The alert value 1.05 is just over the threshold of 1, so traffic is low and the failure repeats every time.

**Logs (Loki)**
- All 5 ERROR records have `order_id=express-1002`, `exception_type=ValueError`, `exception_message="day is out of range for month"`.
- The one successful lookup in the window is `standard-1001` (19:51:15, 200, 5.0 ms). It came one second after three failed `express-1002` lookups (19:51:14), so the service itself was healthy.
- The stack trace ends at `/app/app/main.py`, line 186 (`get_order` → `order_detail(row)`), then line 65 (`placed_at.replace(day=placed_at.day + 2)`).

**Traces (Tempo)**
- 5 server spans, `GET /api/orders/{order_id}`: `cff2c7da…`, `5129b539…`, `bff0190f…`, `5845d74c…`, `3f3b09ec…`. All have `order.id=express-1002`, `http.response.status_code=500` and `STATUS_CODE_ERROR`, plus an `exception` event with the same `ValueError`.
- Trace `cff2c7dab785de46ceef2b3e59ff00fe` matches the most recent log record (span `62ec91f77c8df83a`, 20:17:36).
- Span durations (6–129 ms) don't point to a latency or dependency problem. It is a plain exception in application code.

## 3. Root cause

`app/main.py:65`:

```python
estimated_at = placed_at.replace(day=placed_at.day + 2)
```

`datetime.replace(day=…)` only sets the day number. It doesn't roll over into the next month. When `day + 2` is larger than the number of days in that month, it raises `ValueError`. Nothing catches the exception, so it becomes a 500 (`app/main.py:186` → `app/main.py:65`).

**Affected requests:**
- **Only express orders.** The date calculation only runs inside `if order["priority"] == "express"` (`app/main.py:63`). Standard orders (`standard-1001`, `standard-1003`) skip it, which is why they return 200.
- **Only express orders whose `created_at` falls in the last two days of its month** (in February: the 27th–28th, or 28th–29th in a leap year). For every other day, `day + 2` is still a valid date.
- **`express-1002` fails every time.** The seed data at `app/main.py:45`/`:48` sets its `created_at` to the last day of the previous month (`now.replace(day=1) - timedelta(days=1)`, which is 31 August here). That gives `31 + 2 = 33`.
- **Today makes it worse.** It is 30 September, so any express order created today or yesterday hits the bug (30+2 and 29+2 are both past 30).

**Other endpoints affected by the same bug** (the alert doesn't show these, because the middleware only instruments `get_order`, `app/main.py:104-109`):
- `POST /api/orders` with `priority=express` calls `get_order` at `app/main.py:200` **after** the INSERT has been committed. The client gets a 500 even though the order was created. If clients retry, they may create **duplicate orders**.
- `PATCH /api/orders/{id}` for an affected express order commits the status change, then returns a 500 (`app/main.py:214`).
- `GET /api/orders` (list) doesn't call `order_detail`, so it still works.

The existing tests never look up `express-1002` or any express order, so the bug was never caught.

## 4. Fix

Use `timedelta` for the date arithmetic. It's already imported at `app/main.py:5`.

```diff
--- a/app/main.py
+++ b/app/main.py
@@ -62,7 +62,7 @@ def order_detail(row):
     order = as_dict(row)
     if order["priority"] == "express":
         placed_at = datetime.fromisoformat(order["created_at"])
-        estimated_at = placed_at.replace(day=placed_at.day + 2)
+        estimated_at = placed_at + timedelta(days=2)
         order["estimated_delivery"] = estimated_at.date().isoformat()
     return order
```

This keeps the intended meaning ("placed + 2 days") and also handles month ends, year ends and leap years.

**Regression tests** (add to `tests/test_api.py`):

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("created_at", "expected"),
    [
        ("2026-09-15T12:00:00+00:00", "2026-09-17"),  # mid-month
        ("2026-09-30T12:00:00+00:00", "2026-10-02"),  # 30-day month end
        ("2026-08-31T12:00:00+00:00", "2026-09-02"),  # 31-day month end
        ("2026-12-31T12:00:00+00:00", "2027-01-02"),  # year end
        ("2027-02-28T12:00:00+00:00", "2027-03-02"),  # non-leap February
        ("2028-02-28T12:00:00+00:00", "2028-03-01"),  # leap February
    ],
)
def test_express_estimated_delivery_crosses_month_end(created_at, expected):
    row = {"id": "x", "customer": "c", "item": "i", "priority": "express",
           "status": "received", "created_at": created_at}
    assert main.order_detail(row)["estimated_delivery"] == expected


def test_seeded_express_order_lookup(client):
    # express-1002 is seeded on the last day of the previous month.
    response = client.get("/api/orders/express-1002")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert "estimated_delivery" in response.json()
```

The second test fails on the current code on any day, because the seed always uses a month-end date. So it doesn't depend on when CI runs.

## 5. Mitigation (before the fix ships)

- **Ship the one-line fix as a hotfix.** There's no feature flag or config setting that bypasses this code path, and restarting won't help because the failure repeats every time.
- **Tell support and client teams now:** express orders created on 29–30 September (and `express-1002`) can't be viewed. An express `POST` that returns 500 has **still created the order**, so clients shouldn't retry it. Check `GET /api/orders` (which still works) for duplicates, and clean up any duplicates after the fix.
- A `PATCH` on an affected order that returns 500 has also been applied. Operators can confirm the result through the list endpoint.
- I don't recommend changing `created_at` values in the database to work around the bug. It corrupts order history, and the bug will come back at the next month end.
- The problem will ease somewhat tomorrow (1 October), because new express orders will stop hitting it. But orders already placed on 29–30 September will stay broken until the fix ships, and it will happen again at the end of every month.

## 6. Confidence and open questions

**Confidence: high.** The stack trace points to the exact line. The failing input (`express-1002`, seeded on the last day of a month) produces this exception on the current code. The failing and passing orders split exactly along the `priority == "express"` branch.

I couldn't confirm the following:
- **When it started.** The evidence only covers 19:48–20:18. The seeded `express-1002` would have failed whenever anyone looked it up, so the bug probably goes back further. I didn't check older data.
- **Actual impact on `POST` and `PATCH`.** These endpoints aren't instrumented, so I can't tell from telemetry whether any express orders were created today or whether duplicates exist. Querying the `orders` table for `priority='express'` with `created_at` on the 29th/30th would answer this.
- **Whether the estimate should use business days** rather than calendar days. The fix keeps the current calendar-day behaviour.
- I only read the code and didn't run the fix or the tests, because I had read-only access.
